identification: Tray of mixed small items: (1) gilt star-shaped 'REWARD OF MERIT' prize medal with blue enamel band and plain centre, on a ring (likely gilt base metal, possibly gold; unproven); (2) round open crescent-and-flower brooch, rose-coloured metal set with seed pearls and a small green stone (Edwardian style, likely 9ct but unmarked in photo); (3) yellow gold ribbon-twist bar brooch with an oval blue/green opal (solid or doublet); (4) repousse double-flower bar brooch with two red stones (Victorian style, probably pinchbeck/rolled gold); (5) small rose-gold ring with a turquoise and white-stone cluster in a Taylors Jewellers (3 Centenary Arcade, Launceston) bag, with a handwritten note that appears to say the jeweller could not repair it; (6) worn white-metal medal/coin pendant with loop (figure design, illegible); (7) white-metal 'Exhibition Building' medalet dated 1880 (Melbourne International Exhibition type) and two smaller white-metal arms medalets; (8) enamel badges: heart-shaped 'SEMPER PARATUS' Registered General Nurse of Tasmania badge (orange Maltese cross), round 'MISERIS SUCCURRERE DISCO' nurse badge with red centre lettered L?H (probably LGH, Launceston General Hospital), IOOF 'FLT' Odd Fellows badge, and a round enamel 'FLT' badge with eye/triangle; (9) hat pin with pine-cone/thistle style head stuck in a cork.

viewing_check: Look for 9ct/375/15ct marks on the crescent brooch, opal bar and ring, and weigh them. Check if the opal is solid or a doublet (side view). Read the round nurse badge letters (LGH?) and the maker/number on the back of both nurse badges (Stokes; numbered badges can be traced). Check the Reward of Merit medal back for an inscription or silver/gold mark. Read the jeweller's note.
